title: Rose motif — rolled
subtitle: A flat spiral worked flat and rolled into a bud shape, 5 cm across
excerpt: The rolled rose works a long flat strip of shell stitches, then rolls it tightly from the starting end to form a layered bud. No special techniques beyond treble and chain; the roll itself shapes the flower. At 5 cm across it works as a corsage, a bag embellishment, or a garment button cover.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volume 5 (1890), rolled-petal flower chapter (Internet Archive). Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886), crocheted flower section.
heroPrompt: A crochet rolled rose in deep dusty rose DK cotton, 5 cm across, photographed on natural linen in soft daylight. The spiral bud shape clearly visible from above; layers of shell petals wrap the centre.

chartDefinition.title: Rose motif — rolled
chartDefinition.caption: The chart shows the flat strip before rolling. A foundation chain, then three rows of increasing-length shells. The strip is rolled from the short starting end and secured at the base with a tapestry needle.

glossaryTerms.definition: Multiple trebles worked into the same base stitch, fanning outward. In the rolled rose, increasing-length shells on each row give the graduated petal effect.

content.text: The rolled rose begins as a flat strip: a 36-chain foundation, then two rows of
shell

stitches where the shells in row 2 are larger than the shells in row 1. Rolling the strip tightly from the short end automatically stacks the larger outer shells around the smaller inner shells, creating the layered-petal look without any three-dimensional joining techniques.

The strip must be rolled evenly: too loose and the rose is open and floppy; too tight and the base buckles. A good rule is to roll until the spiral feels firm but the petals can still move slightly. Secure through the base layers with a tapestry needle rather than trying to slip stitch — the needlework hold is more adjustable.

attrs.title: Materials for one rose
attrs.body: About 8 g of DK-weight cotton in a single colour or two tones (lighter colour for the inner rows, darker for the outer). A 4 mm crochet hook. Tapestry needle. Scissors.

content.text: Gauge
Each finished rolled rose measures 5 cm across in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook.
Stitches used
chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st) — UK and US shared.
double crochet (dc) — UK; US "single crochet".
treble (tr) — UK; US "double crochet".
shell (5tr or 7tr into the same st) — multiple trebles fanning outward.
Pattern
Foundation row
Ch 36. Dc into 2nd ch from hook and into every ch to end. (35 dc.) Turn.
Row 2 — small shells (inner petals)
Ch 1 (does not count as stitch). *Work 5tr into next dc (shell made). Sk 1dc. Sl st into next dc.* Repeat from * to * to end of row. Approximately 9 shells. Turn.
Row 3 — large shells (outer petals)

Work into the foundation row only (the dc row), inserting the hook into the dc below the sl-st connector of each shell: *Work 7tr into the dc below the sl st. Sl st into the dc below the centre of the next shell.* Repeat from * to * to end. Approximately 9 large shells. Fasten off, leaving a 30 cm tail.
Rolling

Starting from the short starting end, roll the strip tightly with the right side (shells facing) on the outside of the roll. Hold the base as you roll to keep the layers even. Thread the 30 cm tail through a tapestry needle and take 4 to 5 stitches through the base of the coil to hold the shape. Weave the tail through the base and trim.

definition.title: Rose motif — rolled
definition.caption: Flat strip before rolling. Row 1: 35dc foundation. Row 2: 5tr shells. Row 3: 7tr shells worked into the same foundation row.

content.text: Finishing

The rose can be sewn directly onto a garment or cushion cover through its flat base. For a brooch, sew a brooch pin through the base. For a bag embellishment, anchor through the bottom two coil layers only so the outer petals remain free.
Care
Handwash in cool water with mild soap. Lay flat on a towel and reshape the spiral while damp.
What to try next

The layered rose (crochet-rose-layered) builds separate petal layers and sews them together rather than rolling a single strip. The freestanding rose (crochet-rose-freestanding) is worked fully in the round and stands upright without being attached to a surface.
